author: Simplilearn
description:
If you want a data or backend job by 2026, SQL is your first non‑negotiable skill. Start with the basics: understand what databases are, how tables, rows, and columns work, and practice simple queries using tools like MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQLite. In the first 2–3 weeks, focus only on core syntax: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, and logical filters like AND/OR until you can comfortably answer real questions from a table.

Next, move into data manipulation and summarising: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, plus aggregates like COUNT, SUM, AVG with GROUP BY and HAVING to answer “how many”, “how much”, and “on average” questions. Then tackle joins (INNER, LEFT as a must, RIGHT/FULL later) so you can combine multiple tables, followed by subqueries and CTEs for cleaner, readable logic on more complex problems.

In the next phase, learn basics of schema design (primary/foreign keys, normalization) and indexing so your queries stay fast as data grows this is crucial for data engineering and backend rol
title: SQL for Beginners Roadmap 2026: From Zero to Job‑Ready #simplilearn #shorts

Becoming a Data Scientist isn’t about knowing everything — it’s about mastering the right skills. 

In this video, we’ll break it down super simple.

First skill — Python.
If you want to enter data science, Python is your best friend. You’ll use it to clean data, analyze it, and build models. Almost everything starts here.

Second — SQL.
Data lives inside databases. If you don’t know SQL, you won’t know how to pull the data you need. SQL helps you ask questions to large datasets and get answers fast.

Third — Data Cleaning and Manipulation.
And trust me… data is always messy. Always. That’s where tools like Pandas and NumPy come in. They help you clean, filter, and structure your data properly.

Now comes the exciting part — Machine Learning.
This is where you build models, make predictions, and find patterns. This is the core of data science.

And finally — Data Visualization.
